source.title: Differentiable Faithfulness Alignment for Cross-Model Circuit Transfer
source.authors: Shun Shao; Binxu Wang; Shay B. Cohen; Anna Korhonen; Yonatan Belinkov

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses a different method—learned node-score alignment and CPR evaluation—to test whether IOI circuits transferred across models recover target-model behavior. It does not reproduce the original GPT-2 head-level analysis.
record.gate_note: The paper evaluates IOI circuit faithfulness across model pairs, but does not analyze GPT-2 small's 26 heads or their named roles. IOI values below are the best DFA results across transfer settings, as summarized in Table 18. Control results are not separate rows because they are not IOI circuit outcomes under the learned alignment; cited results from other papers are also excluded.
record.test_reason: This is a methods paper. It learns a mapping (DFA) that projects node-attribution scores from a small model into a larger one, then reports CPR faithfulness of the projected circuits against random alignment and direct target attribution. IOI is one of six MIB tasks used to benchmark that method. The paper never identifies head classes or roles (duplicate-token, S-inhibition, name-mover) in any model. It does not examine the GPT-2 small circuit. W is trained with a faithfulness loss on the target model itself, so a high CPR shows the method works, not that the same circuit recurs. The rows are the study's own method compared with baselines, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that source-model circuits can partially recover faithful target-model circuits, strongest on Llama-3 1B→3B and weaker for larger gaps and Qwen-2.5. The conclusion is stated across six tasks, not for IOI specifically. For IOI the best transfer was Llama-3 3B→8B with NAP-IG-Inputs (0.57). For several Qwen IOI settings, direct target attribution itself was at the random level (0.25).
record.recipe_differences: The paper learns a differentiable source-to-target mapping from node attribution scores and evaluates retained-node circuits with CPR; it does not use the original GPT-2 small head-by-head circuit analysis or its criteria.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported IOI CPR varies with source attribution method and source-target model pair; the paper also reports transfer performance across in-distribution, near-distribution, and zero-shot settings, but Table 18 gives best results across these settings rather than IOI values for each setting separately.

fits_no_version.finding: Node-level IOI attribution scores from a smaller Llama-3/Qwen-2.5 model, mapped by a learned matrix, give target circuits above random CPR. Example: Llama-3 3B→8B NAP-IG-Inputs scores 0.57 vs gold 0.63. Qwen-2.5 transfer is near random.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: IOI-relevant node importance is partially predictable across model sizes within a family via learned functional alignment, without identifying matched head roles.

record.problems: The evidence is limited to node-level circuit scores and CPR, not a head-role analysis. IOI recovery is often far below the direct target-attribution reference; Table 18 gives no uncertainty for these IOI values. The paper does not test prompt variants or GPT-2 small.
record.rows_left_out: No IOI results were left out from Appendix Table 18. Other tasks, control comparisons, and additional transfer-setting results were omitted because they do not measure the IOI outcome for this claim version or duplicate the IOI best-alignment summary.

untested.parts: All: GPT-2 small, 26 heads, 7 classes, faithfulness/completeness/minimality.
All: name-mover ablation and backup-head self-repair.
All: no head classes or roles identified in Llama-3/Qwen-2.5; component reuse across tasks is not measured as shared IOI components.
All: no comparison of recovered circuits to the IOI circuit.
All: no variation of ablation, metric or prompt distribution for the IOI circuit.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V3 labels were dropped. The rows compare the study's own method with baselines. The W matrix is optimized on the target model's faithfulness, so transfer success does not show circuit sameness. On Qwen IOI, gold CPR of 0.25 equals random, so the attribution methods themselves failed there. The 'IOI circuit' here is the set of top-k attributed nodes, not the Wang et al. circuit.

versions.untested_parts: GPT-2 small, the 26 attention heads and 7 classes, their stated roles, and the original faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria.
Ablating the main name-mover heads and measuring backup-head self-repair.

The study tests IOI circuit faithfulness after transfer across model sizes and families, but does not establish that transferred components have the same head-class identities or roles as in GPT-2 small, or test component reuse across other tasks.
Whether other circuit-finding methods, ablation types, or metrics recover essentially the same original circuit.

The study varies transfer settings, attribution methods, and model pairs, but does not test sensitivity of the original circuit's faithfulness/completeness to ablation type, evaluation metric, or prompt distribution, nor whether that circuit explains only part of GPT-2 small's behavior.
The study does not vary IOI name order, templates, number of names, or prompt formats.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: IOI transfer results with CPR above 0.25 (rows r01–r10 and r12–r18)
reader_labels.reason: DFA-aligned circuits exceed the random-alignment reference in these settings, indicating some functional IOI circuit transfer; these results do not identify matching head classes or roles.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: All tested IOI model-pair and attribution-method settings
reader_labels.reason: Recovery is incomplete and often substantially below direct target attribution; one setting matches the random reference, and the study does not test identity of the original head classes or their roles.
